idea-plugin.name: SQL String Concatenation Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags SQL queries built by unparameterized string concatenation or interpolation -- the classic SQL-injection shape -- in Java, Kotlin, and Python, and offers a real quick-fix toward parameterization.

What triggers it (both conditions required):

  • A string literal that looks like the start of a real SQL statement (SELECT/INSERT/ UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/ WITH), combined via + concatenation or string-template/f-string interpolation with a non-constant operand -- e.g. "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + userId (Java/Kotlin), "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $userId" (Kotlin template), f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}" (Python), or "... WHERE id = %s" % user_id.
  • The resulting string is used near a call that looks like it executes SQL: Statement.executeQuery/executeUpdate/execute, cursor.execute/executemany (Python DB-API), and similar conventions (.query(...), .rawQuery(...)).

What does NOT trigger it (the anti-false-positive design, see README for the full worked list):

  • Two constant string literals concatenated ("SELECT * FROM " + "users") -- just code formatting, no variable involved.
  • A SQL-keyword-shaped string with no nearby execution call -- a log message, a comment, a test fixture that's never actually run.
  • A value already parameterized correctly (? placeholders with PreparedStatement.setX(...), or a DB-API parameter tuple like cursor.execute(query, (param,))).

Quick-fix, honest scope: replaces the interpolated value with a ? placeholder and adds a TODO(sql-concat) comment naming the variable that still needs to be bound as a real parameter (.setString(1, ...)/cursor.execute(query, (param,))). It does not infer the value's real type or its correct positional index across a multi-placeholder query -- that's flagged honestly as future work, not silently pretended to be handled.

Deliberately narrow (not a full SAST scanner like Qodana): one specific pattern, near-zero configuration, tuned hard against false positives.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no popups.
